messages:
ellie: quick thread re: hybrid MIG-slice + burst-credit idea. post-canary we saw tiny tenants starving and lots of MIG fragmentation. thinking a single admission layer that understands both slice-affinity and global burst credits could help.

noah: sketch?

ellie: idea: allocate two admission classes per shard: SLICE (pack into reserved MIG slices, non-preemptible while active) and POOL (normal shared slots, preemptible). both draw from a per-region burst credit pool for short spikes.

priya: how do we prevent SLICE from being overallocated and fragmenting nodes? need packing policy and a reclaim path when SLICEs go cold.

ellie: yep. SLICE grants should be lease-based with TTL and heartbeat. controller attempts to pack by tenant-size heuristic; if packing fails, fall back to POOL. reclaim when heartbeat misses > idle_ttl. controller emits "slice_allocated" and "slice_reclaimed" events.

zack: sounds good. what about cross-shard fairness? a tenant could claim many slices across shards to game latency.

ellie: enforce per-tenant slice_quota and region_slice_budget. quota enforced by operator and autoscaler comparing requested slices vs budget atomically. also add a sliding-window rightsize job.

orch-bot: note: operator v0.9 supports slab leases and emits k8s events: Event(SliceAllocated tenant=foo, shard=1, slice_id=foo-1)

noah: burst credits: central token bucket per-region that both SLICE and POOL admission consume. refill rate tuned by capacity. if credits exhausted, POOL admits degrade to queued probes; SLICE requests still allowed only if they came from existing leases.

priya: what about preemption smoothing? we still saw oscillation when credits refill then exhaust quickly. a leaky-bucket smoothing layer could apply to eviction rate and admission ramp.

ellie: propose leaky bucket params and backoff windows:

priya: + config snippet pls.

ellie: ```yaml
admission_policy:
  region_burst:
    token_rate: 100
    bucket_capacity: 500
  slice_class:
    min_lease_slots: 1
    max_lease_slots: 4
    idle_ttl_seconds: 1800
    per_tenant_quota: 2
  smoothing:
    eviction_leaky_bucket_rate: 2 # evictions/sec
    admission_ramp_ms: 500
```

zack: nice. operator api changes? need endpoints to query slice status and force-reclaim.

ellie: yes: GET /operator/v1/slices?region=eu, POST /operator/v1/slices/<id>/reclaim?force=true. reclaim triggers annotated drain and emits events.

noah: rollout plan? can we dogfood region by region behind feature flag and watch metrics: slice_fragmentation_ratio, burst_credit_used_pct, admission_path{slice,pool,queue}, eviction_smoothing_drops.

priya: tests: unit admit logic + property tests simulating 100 tenants with mixed burstiness. integration: staging cluster with synthetic clients that alternate 30s spikes and long tails. measure p50/p95 coldstart and preemption_rate.

zack: ops playbook for emergency: 1) disable slice allocations (--feature slices=false) 2) trigger reclaimed sweeper 3) raise burst refill temporarily 4) if still overloaded, evict low-priority slices by age.

orch-bot: deploy-note: admission-controller v1.6 will log admission_path in traces. sample: "admit: tenant=foo path=slice credit_used=5"

ellie: telemetry knobs: add metric slice_active_slots, slice_idle_seconds, region_burst_tokens, eviction_leaky_rate_actual. dashboards per-region.

noah: one more: packing algorithm should be placement-aware (gpu type + mig tile sizes). fallback to best-effort packing when exact fit not possible. need scheduler hook.

priya: agree. i'll draft an interface for scheduler hook: ScorePlacement(tenant_size, available_nodes) -> node_priority list.

ellie: ok action items: priya -> scheduler hook sketch + tests; noah -> burst-token simulation harness; zack -> operator reclaim endpoints + events + sample kubectl commands; ellie -> PR for admission DSL and rollout checklist. i'll open the thread PR and flag owners.

zack: noted, will start on operator side.

priya: i'll sync with infra about MIG packing constraints.

noah: i'll wire harness and run 24h microbench in staging.

ellie: thanks all. will post follow-ups and link PRs here. :rocket:
